date_note: Money Today reports the drill took place on 25 November.
exec: Korean regulators rehearsed a bank crisis that combines cyberattacks, including AI-enabled ones, and a digital bank run.
geo_basis: Drill held at the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation in Jung-gu, Seoul, per Money Today
plain: South Korea's financial regulators ran a joint crisis drill with major banking groups, using a scenario that included cyberattacks, including AI-enabled ones, and a digital bank run.
summary: According to Money Today, South Korea's Financial Services Commission, with the Financial Supervisory Service, the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Bank of Korea, held a drill with the financial holding companies KB, Shinhan, Hana, Woori and NH and their subsidiary banks. Money Today says it was the first joint drill linking self-rehabilitation and resolution plans. The scenario combined recession and high interest rates with cyberattacks, including AI-enabled ones, and a digital bank run.
title: South Korean regulators hold joint crisis drill with major banks, including AI-enabled cyberattack and digital bank run scenario

validation.note: Only Money Today was read; no regulator release was read.

review.note: stronger than source: first joint crisis drill narrowed to first joint drill linking self-rehab and resolution plans; wrong capital restoration removed; agencies named
